title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Air Force scrambles against air threats
sections.summary: The Singapore Air Force scrambled fighters on 13 February against a suspicious aircraft and yearly responds to over 350 suspicious air threats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Chairman, on 13 February this year, the Singapore Air Force scrambled our fighter aircraft in response to a suspicious aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In any given year, our Air Force response to and investigates more than 350 suspicious air threats in order to protect Singapore's skies.

sections.label: Pandemic disrupts SAF training readiness
sections.summary: The pandemic disrupted SAF operational readiness, deferring NS training and severely curtailing local and overseas training and exercises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The pandemic has disrupted many aspects of SAF operational readiness, including training and exercises – both local and overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: NS training was deferred for an extended period of time, and overseas training and exercises had been severely curtailed.

sections.label: Question on MINDEF pandemic readiness
sections.summary: A question asks the Minister for Defence how MINDEF and the SAF maintained operational readiness during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence provide an account of how the MINDEF as well as the Singapore Armed Forces has maintained operational readiness to keep Singapore safe, even amidst the pandemic?

sections.label: Residents' feedback on RSAF aircraft noise
sections.summary: Members of Parliament from both sides received increased residents' feedback about noise and vibrations from RSAF aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I believe Members of Parliament from both sides of the House have received increased residents' feedback about noise and vibrations from RSAF aircraft.

sections.label: Residents' feedback on flight noise
sections.summary: Residents' feedback includes early morning and night flight times and powerful planes at low altitudes leaving homes vibrating.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Feedback from residents include early morning and night flight times and how the more powerful planes at low altitudes leave homes vibrating in their wake.

sections.label: Question on extent of local training
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to elaborate on the extent of local training today, agreeing on the first two principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While we agree on the first two principles, could the Minister elaborate on the extent of local training today?

sections.label: COVID-19 safety for servicemen
sections.summary: Asks what precautionary measures keep servicemen safe from COVID-19 and how effective they have been.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As our servicemen and women continue to discharge their core mission to defend our home, what are the precautionary measures that have been implemented to keep them safe from COVID-19, and how effective have these measures been?

sections.label: Recalling NSmen as COVID-19 stabilises
sections.summary: Asks what plans MINDEF/SAF have to progressively recall NSmen in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the COVID-19 situation stabilises, what plans does MINDEF/SAF have to progressively recall NSmen in the coming year?

sections.label: SAF flexible responses and NSmen pool
sections.summary: States the SAF must execute flexible, calibrated, sustainable responses, and that the full-time NSmen pool will decrease by a third by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The SAF must also be capable of executing flexible and calibrated responses, and do so in a sustainable manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It has been identified before that the full-time national servicemen pool will decrease by a third by 2030.

sections.label: Fourth IR technology for SAF
sections.summary: States Fourth IR technology such as AI, robotics, data analytics and IoT offers the SAF more efficient and effective training and operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Fourth IR technology such as Artificial intelligence, Robotics, Data Analytics and the Internet of Things offers the SAF the opportunity to conduct its training and operations in a more efficient and effective manner.

sections.label: UNOCT report on ISIS regrouping
sections.summary: States UNOCT reported that ISIS efforts to regroup and reinvigorate activities have gained momentum amidst the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: The UN Office Of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT) reported earlier this month that ISIS’ efforts to regroup and reinvigorate its activities have been gaining momentum amidst the pandemic.

sections.label: ISIS recruitment in Southeast Asia
sections.summary: States Southeast Asia remains a key ISIS recruitment target, citing the August 2020 Sulu bombings and a Malaysian man's deportation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Southeast Asia remains a key target for ISIS recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: This was, perhaps, most apparent in August 2020 when two female suicide bombers self-detonated in the Philippine city of Sulu amidst the height of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Closer to home, the recent news of the deportation of a Malaysian man with alleged links to ISIS also shows the need to continually guard against external threats.

sections.label: Integrated cyber command plans
sections.summary: The Minister for Defence spoke at last year's COS debate about plans to build an integrated cyber command and cyber force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: At the COS debate last year, the Minster for Defence spoke about our plans to build an integrated cyber command and cyber force to protect Singapore’s interests in the digital domain.

sections.label: Military cybersecurity update request
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for Defence for an update on enhancing military cybersecurity and on NSRC initiatives and servicemen's contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In view of this, I would like to ask the Minister for Defence for an update on our effort to enhance our military’s cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry provide an update on initiatives that the NSRC has been working on and, in particular, plans to make the most of the contributions of our servicemen?

sections.label: Supporting NS morale and deployment
sections.summary: The speaker says morale and motivation must be kept high and welcomes the Ministry's announcement on optimising skill-based deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must keep their morale high and motivation strong, supporting them so that their NS involvement through their different life stages will become more engaging, meaningful and fulfilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I welcome the Ministry’s earlier announcement that it would be looking into optimising skill-based deployment.

sections.label: MINDEF environmental sustainability contribution
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MINDEF can update on how MINDEF and SAF contribute to national environmental sustainability efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on how MINDEF and SAF have continued to contribute to our national effort to address environmental sustainability?

sections.label: Work-Study Diploma for NSFs
sections.summary: The speaker notes MINDEF introduced the Work-Study Diploma in September last year for NSFs to train as certified Army and Air Force Technicians.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, amidst a challenging economic context and tight labour market, it is also increasingly important to train and develop our NSFs, as young adults entering the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I was encouraged to learn that in September last year, MINDEF introduced the Work-Study Diploma, also known as WSD, for NSFs to be trained as certified Army and Air Force Technicians while serving their NS.

sections.label: SAF deterrence and birth rate decline
sections.summary: The passage states a strong SAF is a key defence pillar and that Singapore's birth rate saw a 28% drop in live resident births from 1990 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: A strong SAF capable of deterring potential adversaries is a key pillar of Singapore’s defence.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, Singapore’s birth rate has seen a steady decline, seeing a 28% drop in live resident births from 1990 to 2019.

sections.label: Reservist units and fitness criteria
sections.summary: The current reservist system places NSmen in their original NSF units, and physical fitness criteria for deploying NSFs and NSmen in digital, cyber and non-operational roles are to be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, as I understand, the current reservist system places our NSmen in their original units which they began as NSFs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The second consideration is to review the physical fitness criteria in the deployment of our NSFs and NSmen for new, evolving roles in SAF in digital, cyber and non-operational competencies.

sections.label: NSRC deployment initiatives update
sections.summary: The Minister is asked for an update on NSRC initiatives to better deploy servicemen based on civilian expertise to match SAF's evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update on the initiatives that the NSRC has been working on to better deploy our servicemen based on their civilian expertise to match with SAF’s ever evolving needs?

sections.label: External Review Panel tenure
sections.summary: The second External Review Panel on SAF Safety, inaugurated in 2017, would have completed its three-year tenure last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The second External Review Panel on SAF Safety would was inaugurated in 2017 would have completed its three-year tenure last year.

sections.label: SAF IGO audit cycle
sections.summary: Since its formation in 2019 after training accidents, the SAF IGO would have completed its first two-year cycle of audits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Since its formation in 2019 in the aftermath of training accidents, the SAF IGO would have completed its first two-year cycle of audits.

sections.label: Peacetime NS compensation benchmark
sections.summary: In peacetime, the Government is urged to benchmark compensation using projected lifetime income from actual civilian wages of NSmen times remaining work life, and $1 million for NSF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In peacetime situations, I urge the Government to benchmark compensation according to a reasonable projection of lifetime income based on actual civilian wages of NSmen multiplied by their remaining work life, and $1 million for NSF.

sections.label: Insurance cover for operationally-ready NSmen
sections.summary: It is asked whether the current $150,000 Group Term Life and Group Personal Accident insurance covers operationally-ready National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, does the current $150,000 Group Term Life and Group Personal Accident insurance cover operationally-ready National Servicemen?

sections.label: Death and disability coverage
sections.summary: Asks whether coverage can be increased for death or total permanent disability, and what factors apply to lump sum disability compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there room to increase it to provide better coverage in the event of death or total permanent disability of the servicemen?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And third, what are the factors considered for the lump sum disability compensation in the case of permanent disability?

sections.label: Employment support for NSmen
sections.summary: Urges MINDEF to extend career guidance, counselling, employment support, skills training advisories and financial assistance schemes to NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: For those looking for employment in the current economic climate, they will encounter many obstacles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: I strongly urge MINDEF to extend career guidance, counselling and employment support to our NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Will MINDEF consider providing them with post-NS skills training advisories?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Some those who face financial difficulties, what kind of assistance schemes can they tap upon and would the Ministry provide grants or interim loans to help them pay for their studies, training or family expenses and to tide them over this difficult period?

sections.label: PREP4NS physical fitness effectiveness
sections.summary: Asks how effective the PREP4NS initiative has been in helping pre-enlistees become more physically fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: How effective has the PREP4NS initiative been in helping pre-enlistees become more physically fit?

sections.label: NSRC progress and initiatives
sections.summary: Asks for an update on the NSRC's progress and initiatives making NS processes more accessible and convenient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share an update on the NSRC's progress and specifically, about some initiatives that the NSRC has been working on to make NS processes more easily accessible and convenient for pre-enlistees, NSF and NSmen?

sections.label: Strengthening Digital Defence
sections.summary: Asks how MINDEF/SAF is strengthening Digital Defence to prevent online falsehoods from damaging society and communal cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Two years ago, the sixth pillar of Total Defence – Digital Defence – was launched in recognition of the increasing pace of global digitalisation and with this, the growing threats in this domain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: How is MINDEF/SAF strengthening Digital Defence to prevent online falsehoods from damaging our society and eroding communal cohesion?

sections.label: Climate Defence as Total Defence pillar
sections.summary: Asks whether MINDEF will consider adopting Climate Defence as a new pillar of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Given the nature of the required approach, will MINDEF consider adopting Climate Defence as a new pillar of Total Defence?

sections.label: Digital Defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: Digital Defence was introduced as the sixth pillar in 2019 in recognition of new threats from increasing digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: In recognition of the new waves of threats brought about by increasing digitalisation, Digital Defence was introduced as the sixth pillar in 2019.

sections.label: Climate Defence pillar question
sections.summary: A question asks whether MINDEF will consider adopting Climate Defence as a new Total Defence pillar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Given the nature of the required approach, will MINDEF consider adopting Climate Defence as the new pillar of Total Defence?

sections.label: SG Together engagement sessions
sections.summary: SG Together began Emerging Stronger Conversations in August 2020, and Dr Maliki Osman said MINDEF would hold engagement sessions under the movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: The SG Together movement has initiated Singapore Together Emerging Stronger Conversations in August 2020, where views may differ but all strive towards a common goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply last year, then Senior Minister of State for Defence Dr Maliki Osman spoke about how MINDEF would conduct a series of engagement sessions as part of the SG Together movement to hear Singaporeans on how all of us can do better to put Total Defence in action.

sections.label: Engagement session outcomes question
sections.summary: A question asks what the outcomes of the engagement sessions are and how MINDEF will take public views forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: What are the outcomes from these engagement sessions and how will MINDEF take public views and suggestions forward?

sections.label: MINDEF empowering Singaporeans question
sections.summary: A question asks how MINDEF is supporting and empowering Singaporeans to play a greater role in Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: How is MINDEF supporting and empowering Singaporeans to play an even greater role in Total Defence so that the country can emerge stronger together?

sections.label: MINDEF budget growth
sections.summary: MINDEF's budget will see double-digit growth, mainly because it spent about $1.5 billion less than planned in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The first obvious fact is that MINDEF's budget will see double-digit growth year on year – not seen since 1998 – but mainly because MINDEF spent about $1.5 billion less than planned in 2020, about 10% less, due to the delay of some projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: If the post-COVID recovery ensues, MINDEF expects its budget to stabilise and return to a growth trajectory targeted and announced in previous years – about 3 to 4% nominal growth each year, to keep pace with inflation over a period.

sections.label: US-China rivalry shifts region
sections.summary: The US-China strategic rivalry will shift the global centre of gravity to the region, physically for defence and security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The US-China strategic rivalry will shift the global centre of gravity to our region, and I mean this physically for defence and security.

sections.label: Quad Exercise Malabar and Asia spending
sections.summary: The Quad conducted Exercise Malabar off India for the first time in 13 years, and Asia's military spending is 40% higher than Europe's.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Quad – Australia, India, Japan and the United States – conducted Exercise Malabar off the coast of India for the first time in 13 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I have previously furnished details of Asia's military spending, which surpassed Europe's a decade ago and is now 40% higher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Asia's military spending is 40% higher than Europe's.

sections.label: Shoalwater Bay and Greenvale construction
sections.summary: The expanded Shoalwater Bay and Greenvale Training Areas are under construction, on track for completion by 2024 and 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For defence, the expanded Shoalwater Bay Military Training Area and the Greenvale Training Area are under construction and on track to being completed by 2024 and 2028 respectively.

sections.label: DSO PCR tests operational
sections.summary: Within the same month, DSO got the polymerase chain reaction tests up and running, fully operational.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Within the same month, DSO managed to get the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests up and running, fully operational.

sections.label: RESOLUTE 2.0 PCR kits available
sections.summary: DSO and A*STAR's RESOLUTE 2.0 PCR kits are commercially available and will be used with automation for about 4,000 tests a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: DSO and A*STAR's RESOLUTE 2.0 PCR kits are now commercially available and will be used with automation to conduct about 4,000 tests a day for the whole of Government.

sections.label: DSO and Medical Corps personnel
sections.summary: Investments maintained 40 bio-personnel in DSO and about 250 doctors and paramedical staff in the Medical Corps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have kept up our investments to maintain 40 bio-personnel in DSO – not a large number, 40 – and about 250 doctors and paramedical staff in the Medical Corps.

sections.label: OPCW labs and DSO
sections.summary: There are only 12 OPCW-designated labs able to verify chemical agents in environmental and biomedical samples, and DSO is one of them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Some examples are chlorine, sulfur mustard, sarin and even Novichok.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: There are only 12 OPCW-designated labs around the world capable of verifying chemical agents in both environmental and biomedical samples; and DSO is one of them.

sections.label: MINDEF biological threat capabilities
sections.summary: Learning from the pandemic, MINDEF will further build up its laboratories and capabilities to deal with biological threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As Dr Wan Rizal asked, what can we learn from this?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I think learning from this pandemic, MINDEF will further build up our laboratories and capabilities to deal with biological threats.

sections.label: DSO BSL-4 upgrade funding
sections.summary: MINDEF will invest about $90 million for DSO, working with MOH, to upgrade its facilities to the highest biosafety level of BSL-4.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: MINDEF will therefore invest about $90 million for DSO working with MOH to upgrade our facilities within DSO to the highest biosafety level of BSL-4.

sections.label: COVID-19 MINDEF/SAF personnel deployment
sections.summary: At the height of COVID-19 efforts, over 6,000 MINDEF/SAF personnel were deployed across a wide range of operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: At the height of our efforts against COVID-19, we deployed over 6,000 MINDEF/SAF personnel across a wide range of operations that Members of Parliament here described in your speeches.

sections.label: In-Camp Training resumption
sections.summary: In-Camp Trainings have picked up to 80% of pre-COVID levels and are expected to resume fully by the later half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Locally, In-Camp Trainings (ICTs) have progressively picked up, up to 80% of pre-COVID levels – I think Mr Abdul Samad asked this – and are expected to resume fully by the later half of this year.

sections.label: Local training flight sorties
sections.summary: Since October last year, local training flights were brought down to pre-pandemic levels, an average of 600 sorties each month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Since October last year, we have brought down the number of local training flights to what they were before the pandemic – an average of 600 sorties each month.

sections.label: SAF progress despite COVID-19 delays
sections.summary: The SAF remains on track despite some delays due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Despite some delays due to COVID-19, the SAF remains on track, I am happy to report.

sections.label: RSAF new helicopters and F-35s
sections.summary: The RSAF will receive H225M and CH-47F helicopters this year, four F-35s around 2026, and train in Guam from 2029.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The RSAF will also receive new helicopters this year – H225Ms to replace our Super Pumas and our Chinook 47Fs (CH-47Fs) to replace our older Chinooks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We remain on track to receive four F-35 Joint Strike Fighters around 2026 and for the RSAF to start basing their training in Guam from 2029 onwards.

sections.label: Counter-Terrorism Information Facility established
sections.summary: MINDEF decided to stand up a multilateral Counter-Terrorism Information Facility to close the gap and pre-empt terror attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: To close the gap and pre-empt terror attacks, MINDEF decided to stand up a multilateral Counter-Terrorism Information Facility (CTIF).

sections.label: MINDEF Commercial Cloud rollout
sections.summary: A MINDEF Commercial Cloud will roll out in mid-2021, starting with administrative and maintenance functions, benefiting NSFs and NSmen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: First, a MINDEF Commercial Cloud will roll out in mid-2021, starting with just administrative and maintenance functions, and this will benefit NSFs and NSmen with better and more responsive services.

sections.label: SAF hiring more cyber-specialists
sections.summary: The SAF will hire more cyber-specialists as regulars, mainly through the Military Domain Expert Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In addition, the SAF will hire more cyber-specialists as regulars, mainly through our Military Domain Expert Scheme.

sections.label: Updated Medical Classification System
sections.summary: The SAF will use an updated Medical Classification System, which with its PES system will better match vocations and deployment of National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Moving forward, the SAF will use an updated and refreshed Medical Classification System, which together with its PES system, will better match vocations and deployment of National Servicemen.

sections.label: MINDEF SAF emissions targets
sections.summary: MINDEF and SAF will cut emissions growth by two-thirds by 2030 and halve 2030 emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: MINDEF and SAF have gone through a thorough evaluation of our carbon and waste footprint and determined that we can meet and in major areas exceed, the national targets set under the SGP30.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: By 2030, MINDEF and SAF will reduce the growth of overall emissions by two-thirds compared to business as usual, using current systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: By 2050, we aim to halve the 2030 emissions in line with our national strategy.

sections.label: Green buildings and solar panels
sections.summary: MINDEF aims for Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy buildings and will double solar adoption in SAF camps by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For buildings, we aim to attain the Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy standards for all new large and retrofitted buildings where feasible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We will also deploy more solar panels in SAF camps and bases by 2025 so that our solar adoption will be doubled, from 20 to 50 mega-watt peak, equivalent to the electricity consumed by 12,500 4-room households.

sections.label: Smart utility metering systems
sections.summary: MINDEF and SAF will install smart utility metering systems so unit commanders can track emissions, waste and water use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And central to this strategy is for each unit to know how much it produces in emissions and waste or water consumption – just imagine if we ask our population to save water or electricity without measuring it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Therefore, MINDEF and SAF will install smart utility metering systems progressively for all our buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This will allow commanders of each unit to take ownership and give directions to make the SAF greener.

sections.label: New SAF Sustainability Office
sections.summary: MINDEF will set up a new SAF Sustainability Office reporting to the Chief of Staff-Joint Staff as Chief Sustainability Officer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: MINDEF has, therefore, decided to set up a new SAF Sustainability Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It will report to the SAF's Chief of Staff-Joint Staff, who will assume the role of the SAF Chief Sustainability Officer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The office will be advised by an External Advisory Panel made up of experts in various fields.

sections.label: Strengthening National Service
sections.summary: NS remains the backbone of defence and the NS Review Committee was established last year to strengthen it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: NS continues to be the backbone of our defence and we must strengthen NS for our Next-Gen SAF and a new generation of National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We established the NS Review Committee, or NSRC, last year precisely with this in mind.

sections.label: Redesigning PES classification
sections.summary: The medical classification and PES system are being redesigned to move away from binary combat-fit classification for deployment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This again, the Minister for Defence has mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We are redesigning our medical classification system and the Physical Employment Standard or PES System, to shift away from the binary classification of a serviceman either as combat-fit or not combat-fit for purposes of deployment.

sections.label: First servicemen batch programme
sections.summary: The first batch of 37 servicemen will commence this programme this April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The first batch of 37 servicemen will commence this programme this April.

sections.label: Expanding NSmen deployment opportunities
sections.summary: We will expand opportunities to deploy NSmen with civilian expertise, increase deployment areas, and establish a dedicated deployment centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Moving forward, we will systematically expand opportunities to deploy NSmen with relevant civilian expertise and we will increase the areas they can be deployed to and establish a dedicated deployment centre to oversee this expansion.

sections.label: External safety experts tapped
sections.summary: MINDEF established the first External Review Panel on SAF Safety in 2013 to have safety experts assess SAF safety systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In enhancing these areas, we have continued to tap on external safety experts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This started in 2013, when MINDEF established the first External Review Panel on SAF Safety, or ERPSS, to have safety experts from academia and the industry provide an independent assessment of the SAF's safety systems and processes.

sections.label: Third ERPSS and SAF IGO
sections.summary: MINDEF commissioned the third ERPSS for three years, and the SAF Inspector-General's Office completed its first two-year audit cycle.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Given the Panel's valuable contributions, MINDEF has accordingly commissioned the third ERPSS for another three-year tenure, beginning this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The SAF Inspector-General's Office, or IGO, was formed in 2019 and it has just completed its full first two-year audit cycle of all SAF formations.

sections.label: Launch use and support
sections.summary: Since its launch in October 2019, it was used and supported 23 overseas exercises and over 2,000 patient encounters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since its launch in October 2019, it was used and has supported 23 overseas exercises and over 2,000 patient encounters.

sections.label: Compensation amounts range
sections.summary: Any compensation amounts are generally between two and four times that provided under the WICA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Any compensation amounts are generally in the area of between two and four times of that provided under the WICA.

sections.label: Compensation for lost earnings
sections.summary: MINDEF will compensate servicemen for lost earnings after release due to medical or hospitalisation leave, up to two years from service end.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Should these servicemen experience a loss of earnings after their release from service as a result of medical or hospitalisation leave, MINDEF will also compensate them for up to two years from the day after their service ends.

sections.label: Financial assistance for NSFs
sections.summary: MINDEF/SAF maintains financial assistance schemes, including ones for immediate acute needs such as sudden family retrenchment, to help NSFs focus on NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: To enable our NSFs to focus on their NS obligations, MINDEF/SAF maintains a variety of financial assistance schemes, including ones designed to support immediate, acute needs, such as a sudden retrenchment in the family.

sections.label: NSFs benefiting since 2015
sections.summary: Over 74,000 NSFs have benefited from these efforts since 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Over 74,000 NSFs have benefited from these efforts since 2015.

sections.label: PREP4NS membership trial
sections.summary: Since its first trial in November 2019, about 5,000 pre-enlistees have been accorded PREP4NS membership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since its first trial in November 2019, about 5,000 pre-enlistees have been accorded the PREP4NS membership.

sections.label: Gold attainment after PREP4NS
sections.summary: Thirty-three percent more pre-enlistees attained a Gold after receiving their PREP4NS membership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Thirty-three percent more pre-enlistees attained a Gold after receiving their PREP4NS membership.

sections.label: Screening and ICT enhancements
sections.summary: IPPT-eligible NSmen aged 35 and above undergo screening for safe ICT participation, with two enhancements benefiting about 11,000 NSmen annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: NSmen who are IPPT-eligible and aged 35 and above undergo screening to ensure that they can safely participate in the more strenuous activities during the ICT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We have introduced two enhancements, which will benefit about 11,000 NSmen annually.

sections.label: Strengthening National Service for Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states NS must be strengthened for a new generation by maximising contributions, improving health and fitness, and enriching experience, with Total Defence as Singapore's best preparation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Our national servicemen are at the heart of our digitalisation drive and we are committed to making NS-related services and processes ever more convenient and seamless.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As the SAF transforms to meet new threats, so must NS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We are committed to strengthening NS for a new generation of servicemen in three ways: maximising their contributions, improving their health and fitness, and enriching their NS experience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We must never forget that NS was designed and put in place for an existential purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We need NS and we need an effective NS in order to safeguard our survival, security, freedom and sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Dr Ng’s speech underlined how we need not just the SAF but all of society to support Singapore’s defence against conventional and non-conventional threats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Total Defence remains Singapore’s best preparation and response to crises.

sections.label: Keeping communities safe, reopening borders
sections.summary: The passage states communities were kept safe with low infections and hospitalisations, putting Singapore in a better position to reopen borders, restart the economy and host major events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The result is that we have been able to keep our communities safe, keep infections and hospitalisations low.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are in a better position today to reopen our borders and restart our economy, and hopefully host major international events such as the Shangri-La Dialogue and the World Economic Forum later this year.

sections.label: ACCORD engagement with youth and women
sections.summary: The passage states ACCORD members identified stepping up engagement with youth and women on defence and NS issues, and raising appreciation for NSmen and employer recognition of their skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: ACCORD members have identified a few, including stepping up engagement with youth and women on defence and National Service issues, raising public appreciation for NSmen and employer recognition of the skills they gain from National Service.

sections.label: Families explore BMTC virtually
sections.summary: The passage states more than 180 families explored the BMTC through an online video and joined a virtual dialogue with senior commanders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: More than 180 families got to explore the BMTC via an online video and engage in a virtual dialogue with senior commanders.

sections.label: Revamped Singapore Discovery Centre opening
sections.summary: The passage announces that a fully revamped Singapore Discovery Centre will open at the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Here, I am happy to announce that a fully revamped Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC) will be opened at the end of this year.

sections.label: Digital Defence in courses and programmes
sections.summary: The passage states that after a pilot with SUSS in 2020, work with ACCORD will reach out to other universities, and Digital Defence is offered at 19 institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Following a successful pilot with SUSS in 2020, we will work with ACCORD to reach out to other Universities to potentially introduce Digital Defence into relevant course modules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Another example is our collaboration with SkillsFuture Singapore, National Library Board and the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore to add a Digital Defence component to the SkillsFuture for the Digital Workplace programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is currently being offered at 19 institutions, including Polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education.

sections.label: Six pillars and pandemic themes
sections.summary: Focus stays on the present six pillars, incorporating pandemic responses and environmental sustainability themes where appropriate within each pillar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For now, we will focus on the present six pillars, and incorporate pandemic responses and environmental sustainability themes, where appropriate, within each pillar.

sections.label: SDC sustainability and defence engagements
sections.summary: The revamped SDC will have a sustainability theme, including over 2,000 solar panels and urban farming education programmes, alongside engagements on defence and NS issues.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Here, I would add that the revamped SDC will have a sustainability theme in its infrastructure and programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: These include the deployment of over 2,000 solar panels to generate power for about half of SDC's electrical consumption; as well as new education programmes on urban farming and sustainability for the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will do so by encouraging Singaporeans to be more active in conversations about defence and NS issues.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that we launched two series of engagements last year, "Strengthening Commitment to Defence" and "Total Defence for a Future Singapore", in conjunction with the Singapore Together Emerging Stronger Conversations.

sections.label: ACCORD content and Alliances for Action
sections.summary: Some efforts go through ACCORD, such as content on National Servicemen's COVID-19 contributions, and exploring Singapore Together Alliances for Action to strengthen Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Some will be taken through ACCORD, such as developing fresh content on how our National Servicemen have contributed to the COVID-19 national response.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We hope that this showcases the invaluable skills and efforts by our National Servicemen and inspires others who have yet to serve National Service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are also exploring forming or tapping on the Singapore Together Alliances for Action (AfAs) that will bring together stakeholders from the Government, businesses and community to follow up on initiatives to strengthen Total Defence and all our support for NS.

sections.label: Investing in Total Defence
sections.summary: Continued investment in Total Defence aims to prepare for, respond to and recover from any crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Your actions have shown that, with everyone doing their part for Total Defence, we will emerge stronger from this crisis of our generation and with greater confidence in our future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is why we continue to invest in Total Defence – to best prepare for, respond to and recover from any crisis.

sections.label: Defence relations and partnerships
sections.summary: Relations with friends, partners and surrounding countries are good, citing the renewed 30-year Memorandum of Understanding with President Trump and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Australia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our relations with our friends, partners and surrounding countries are good.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If I can mention some signature events, I think the renewal of the Memorandum of Understanding which Prime Minister signed with President Trump then was a significant event because that was a 30-year agreement which now is extended.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Australia is certainly a very powerful instrument to build not only defence ties but ties between countries, and as well as physical assets in Shoalwater Bay and Greenvale, and we are committing resources there.

sections.label: NSmen injury compensation and insurance
sections.summary: Injured NSmen receive the same compensation treatment, and MINDEF and SAF periodically review group term insurance coverage amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in response to Mr Gerald Giam's three questions, the first one is whether or not NSmen, should they be injured, whether the treatment with regard to compensation is the same, the answer is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: On his question whether or not the group term insurance payout amounts can be raised, I would like to inform him that MINDEF and SAF do review the quantum of coverage periodically, and we will take into account all relevant factors as we conduct these reviews.
